run.question:
Alertmanager alert KubePodNotReady (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/checkout-7ffc7768f4-64slm since 2026-11-25T11:16:49Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The alert is explained by pod otel-demo/checkout-7ffc7768f4-64slm: it is Pending because its only app container can never start — the container state is waiting with reason ImagePullBackOff, and the kubelet reports ErrImagePull with the registry answer 'not found' for the reference quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-arm64@sha256:20c6ce98bea7470d39364356ec0a8482fa7356ac92e132256539417688da615a. That reference is what the Deployment otel-demo/checkout now carries in its pod template; the ReplicaSet checkout-7ffc7768f4 and its pod were created at 2026-11-25T11:16:34Z, and the Deployment's managed fields show an Update by field manager 'OpenAPI-Generator' at exactly 11:16:34Z on generation 2, distinct from the Helm Apply at 11:13:34Z. Only this one Deployment in the cluster carries a hello-bench image. The old ReplicaSet checkout-64c65899fc and its pod checkout-64c65899fc-qtrbk still run the real image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:3.1.0-checkout (image_id ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo@sha256:d4448ff541290fc57cca71d4bfd35d522959edf62a8bb55158467583f9fad4e2), stay Ready with 0 restarts and remain the service's only ready endpoint, so the checkout Service itself still has one working backend; the impact visible for this cause is the permanently non-ready new pod and the stalled rollout (1 unavailable replica, Progressing/ReplicaSetUpdated). Registry reachability, node scheduling and application startup are all ruled out as causes by direct evidence: the same pod pulled busybox:latest at 11:16:35Z, the pod was Scheduled normally, and the container never started so no application log or readiness probe exists. The agent identification in the evidence is a field manager name, not a Kubernetes object I could read, and no change-history integration is available, so who applied the template change is not verified.

claims.text: Pod otel-demo/checkout-7ffc7768f4-64slm has phase Pending, created 2026-11-25T11:16:34Z, owner ReplicaSet checkout-7ffc7768f4; its conditions are Ready=False and ContainersReady=False while PodScheduled=True, and its container 'checkout' has restartCount 0 and state waiting with reason ImagePullBackOff.

The kubelet's exact pull error for that pod is: failed to pull and unpack image "quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-arm64@sha256:20c6ce98bea7470d39364356ec0a8482fa7356ac92e132256539417688da615a": failed to resolve reference ... not found; events record 5 Failed pulls, 5 'Error: ErrImagePull', 20 BackOff and 20 'Error: ImagePullBackOff' between 2026-11-25T11:16:36Z and 11:21:40Z.

Deployment otel-demo/checkout's pod template container 'checkout' uses image quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-arm64:2.0.0@sha256:20c6ce98bea7470d39364356ec0a8482fa7356ac92e132256539417688da615a, and its status shows replicas 2 with updatedReplicas 1, readyReplicas 1, availableReplicas 1, unavailableReplicas 1 and condition Progressing reason ReplicaSetUpdated last transition 2026-11-25T11:16:34Z.

Deployment checkout owns two ReplicaSets: checkout-64c65899fc (created 11:13:36Z, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:3.1.0-checkout) and checkout-7ffc7768f4 (created 11:16:34Z, image quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-arm64:2.0.0@sha256:20c6...).

Deployment otel-demo/checkout is at generation 2 and its managedFieldsSummary shows helm Apply at 2026-11-25T11:13:34Z and a separate manager 'OpenAPI-Generator' Update at 2026-11-25T11:16:34Z, the same minute the new ReplicaSet and pod were created.
Across all namespaces, otel-demo/checkout is the only Deployment whose container images contain 'hello-bench'; the other 46 Deployments do not carry that image.

The pre-existing pod checkout-64c65899fc-qtrbk is Running and Ready with 0 restarts and image_id ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo@sha256:d4448ff541290fc57cca71d4bfd35d522959edf62a8bb55158467583f9fad4e2, and the checkout Service endpoints list it under addresses while checkout-7ffc7768f4-64slm appears only under notReadyAddresses.

Image retrieval itself worked in the same period: checkout-7ffc7768f4-64slm pulled busybox:latest successfully at 11:16:35Z for its init container, and the other otel-demo pods pulled ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:3.1.0-* images successfully between 11:13 and 11:15Z.

kube_pod_container_info for pod checkout-7ffc7768f4-64slm lists container 'checkout' with image quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-arm64:2.0.0@sha256:20c6... and no image_id field, starting at the 11:17:00Z sample; the same metric for checkout-64c65899fc-qtrbk carries image_id ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo@sha256:d4448ff5...
kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{namespace="otel-demo",deployment="checkout"} read 0 at the 11:14:00Z and 11:15:00Z samples and 1 at the 11:16:00Z through 11:21:00Z samples.

The alerting rule KubePodNotReady (group kubernetes-apps, duration 300s) is firing with activeAt 2026-11-25T11:16:49Z and labels namespace=otel-demo, pod=checkout-7ffc7768f4-64slm; its expression matches kube_pod_status_phase Pending/Unknown or Running with kube_pod_status_ready==0, so a Pending pod satisfies it. The same rule is also firing for an unrelated pod itbench-observability/prometheus-kube-prometheus-stack-prometheus-0.

checkout's own span-status signal shows no error status: sum by (service_name,status_code) increase(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name=~"checkout|payment|frontend"}[3509s]) returned for checkout only status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET (1850.12 span increase) and no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series for checkout (payment likewise UNSET only).

For frontend, the same hour-span query returned status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR with a 530.99 span increase, while sum by (status_code) increase(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend",status_code!="STATUS_CODE_UNSET"}[300s]) returned 0 at both returned sample times 11:16:49Z and 11:21:49Z.

The query over ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config data key demo.flagd.json for flags whose defaultVariant is neither null nor "off" returned no entries, i.e. it matched no enabled fault flag in that file.

All 27 pods in namespace otel-demo other than checkout-7ffc7768f4-64slm were Running with Ready=True and restartCount 0 at the time of the query, including the old checkout pod checkout-64c65899fc-qtrbk.

The Deployment otel-demo/checkout pod template was overwritten with a wrong, non-existent benchmark image reference (quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-arm64:2.0.0@sha256:20c6...), so the new ReplicaSet checkout-7ffc7768f4's pod can never pull and start its container, which is what makes the pod non-ready and keeps the rollout at 1 unavailable replica.

Registry or network outage preventing image pulls is rejected: the same pod pulled busybox:latest successfully at 11:16:35Z, other otel-demo pods pulled their ghcr.io images successfully minutes earlier, and the failure text is the registry's NotFound for one specific digest rather than a timeout or connection error.

Scheduling, resource or quota problems are rejected as the reason this pod is not ready: the pod's PodScheduled condition is True, it was assigned to node kind-environment-worker at 11:16:34Z, and no FailedScheduling event exists for it (FailedScheduling events in the window belong to kube-system and local-path-storage pods).

Application crash or failed readiness probe is rejected as the cause of this pod's non-ready state: the checkout container never started (state waiting/ImagePullBackOff, restartCount 0, no lastState), so no readiness probe or application runtime was reached; the single Unhealthy event in otel-demo is the otel-collector startup readiness probe at 11:13:38Z on otel-collector-74d749ff5f-5vwwt.

A flagd feature-flag fault is rejected as this pod's cause: the flagd-config query found no flag with a non-off defaultVariant, and a feature flag in checkout's runtime cannot prevent the container image from being pulled.

The Helm release change is rejected as the origin of the image change: helm's Apply on this Deployment is recorded at 11:13:34Z, whereas the template-affecting Update recorded at 11:16:34Z belongs to a different manager, 'OpenAPI-Generator', the same minute the new ReplicaSet was created.

gaps: Who or what applied the Deployment checkout template change is not identified: the writer appears only as field manager 'OpenAPI-Generator' in metadata.managedFieldsSummary, no Kubernetes object with that name was found, and the change_history integration is not available for this Run; therefore a deliberate fault injection versus a bad manual/gitops change could not be verified.

The alert's activeAt of 2026-11-25T11:16:49Z is only 15 seconds after the pod was created (11:16:34Z) while the loaded KubePodNotReady rule has duration 300s; why the alert fired so early in the pod's life is not established by the evidence.

Jaeger could not be used: traces_search for service checkout returned HTTP 404 (SOURCE_ERROR) and traces_list_services returned HTTP 404 (INVALID_PARAMS), so there is no trace-level view of checkout's requests; span-status metrics were used instead and counts of spans are not request counts.

The frontend STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans seen in the hour-span aggregate (530.99 span increase) are not attributed: the 5-minute windows ending 11:16:49Z and 11:21:49Z both read 0, and no evidence ties them to the checkout pod or to this image change.

Whether the checkout Service experienced request failures while only one ready endpoint served it was not measured; only endpoint membership (1 ready, 1 not-ready address) and the absence of checkout error-status spans were observed.
The unrelated KubePodNotReady firing for itbench-observability/prometheus-kube-prometheus-stack-prometheus-0 was not investigated.
next_steps: Restore the checkout Deployment pod template image to ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:3.1.0-checkout (as used by ReplicaSet checkout-64c65899fc) so the pending pod can be replaced by a pullable one.

Check the GitOps/automation or agent client that writes as 'OpenAPI-Generator' (and any audit log of API writes at 2026-11-25T11:16:34Z) to confirm how the hello-bench-arm64:2.0.0@sha256:20c6... reference entered the Deployment.
Confirm with the registry (quay.io/it-bench) whether that digest is supposed to exist; the kubelet reported it as not found.

Alert on the stalled rollout condition (Deployment Progressing/ReplicaSetUpdated with unavailable replicas) in addition to pod not-ready so an image-pull failure on a surge pod is visible even while one old replica keeps serving.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.

rules.name: KubePodNotReady
rules.query: sum by (namespace, pod, job, cluster) (max by (namespace, pod, job, cluster) (kube_pod_status_phase{job="kube-state-metrics",namespace=~".*",phase=~"Pending|Unknown"} or (kube_pod_status_phase{job="kube-state-metrics",namespace=~".*",phase="Running"} == 1 and on (namespace, pod, cluster) kube_pod_status_ready{condition="true",job="kube-state-metrics",namespace=~".*"} == 0)) * on (namespace, pod, cluster) group_left () topk by (namespace, pod, cluster) (1, max by (namespace, pod, owner_kind, cluster) (kube_pod_owner{owner_kind!="Job"}))) > 0 unless on (namespace, pod, cluster) kube_pod_status_reason{job="kube-state-metrics",namespace=~".*",reason="SchedulingGated"} == 1
